transcript.text: Bosch WTN85201GB condenser dryer not drying properly anymore, clothes still damp after 2 hrs. any ideas

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. On a Bosch condenser dryer like yours, clothes coming out damp after two hours is most often caused by restricted airflow or how the laundry was prepared. The heat-pump system needs air to flow freely through the lint filter and the condenser unit; if these are clogged with fluff, drying times increase dramatically. Please check the following:
1. Lint Filter: Remove it from the door opening and rinse off any fluff under a tap. Ensure it is completely dry before putting it back.
2. Condenser Unit: Open the flap at the bottom front of the machine, slide out the condenser unit (the stack of plastic fins), and rinse it thoroughly to remove hidden fluff. Let it drip dry for 10–15 minutes before refitting.
3. Load Size & Spin: Ensure you aren't overloading the drum (it should be no more than two-thirds full) that the clothes were spun at a high speed (e.g.Did cleaning the filter and condenser improve the situation, or was one of them particularly clogged?

Yes, it did. The filter had fluff and a waxy film and needed scrubbing before water would go through. The condenser was matted with lint, and I'd never cleaned it, but it rinsed clean. Test cycle afterwards dried in about 100 mins and the container was nearly full. Load was normal and spin 1200.

That is excellent news. The waxy film on the filter was likely from fabric conditioner residue, which traps fluff and severely restricts airflow; keeping that clean will keep drying times short. I would suggest cleaning the condenser every few months to maintain performance. Please let me know if you need anything else.

candidates: Clogged lint filter or condenser restricting airflow (high)
Overloading or laundry not spun well enough in the washer (medium)
Coated moisture sensors causing early termination (low)
